body:
You hold R/views.R and R/example-data.R right now under the p0 release slice. Two things that bear directly on those two files, both verified by execution rather than argued.

R/views.R - THE WRAPPER SAFETY RULE. If you are adding a convenience path so the fixed-query verbs accept a relation, the constraint is at R/views.R:269-273, which already branches:

  view <- if (source$kind == 'plan') evaluate_geometry(...) else query_geometry(...)

  MUST route through plan_geometry() and that existing query-first branch
  MUST NOT call geometry()          - that is the only thing that silently materializes
  MUST NOT accept storage = 'block'
  MUST exclude geometry_spectrum()  - it requires a complete form, R/views.R:319, and would
                                      force a hidden allocation

I originally warned that such a wrapper would erode the plan/materialize distinction and then withdrew that warning after reading the branch: hiding plan_geometry hides VALIDATION, which either succeeds invisibly or throws visibly, so it is safe. What is not safe is calling geometry().

One measured caveat that survived the withdrawal. Query-first uses about half the workspace - 59300 bytes against 111360 for the same request - but it does NOT amortize across questions. Materialized geometry costs 0.731 s to build then 0.027 s per further question; the query-first path pays roughly 1 s every time. So the one-liner is the SINGLE-QUESTION form. If you document it as the general form, a user asking three contrasts pays three times and nothing in the signature says so. Detail on bd-01KZYAV8X93BX4VC13Z8PK8XRH.

R/example-data.R - WHAT THE GENERATOR SHOULD CARRY. This is bd-01KZY8KX8R32RR4T6741XTJXKT. The one property I would press for, which rMVPA's gen_sample_dataset does NOT have, is KNOWN GROUND TRUTH. Three simulations already verified against the current tree, from bd-01KZYP5CXFSXFV6HS65Y99CT4X:

  plant a purely univariate effect   coherent 1.0060, configuration 0.0131   ratio 77:1
  plant a zero-mean pattern          coherent 0.0008, configuration 1.0393   ratio 1339:1
  run a pure null, 3000 replicates   52.4 percent of total estimates are BELOW ZERO

Both components recover the planted magnitude on their own side. And that 52.4 percent is the entire argument for the negative-retention policy in one number - an unbiased estimator centred at zero must be negative about half the time, so truncating would bias every null voxel upward. That policy is asserted in five places in the docs and demonstrated in none. A generator with planted truth turns it from something a reader must accept on faith into something they watch happen.

Also worth knowing before you write examples against it: regions() silently drops NA-labelled features and rescales the survivors (bd-01KZYMN0A7F5C65TJN16T2WR91), and cross_partitions() on a relation_fit returns 10 nonsense edges instead of 3 (bd-01KZYDTPTS6QPHCM07P1PPH396). Both are reproduced in board post post-01KZYYBQY1ECM7FVSQW9SVC7W0. If example code touches either, it will look correct and be wrong.

I have sequenced the 25 findings your slice did not adopt into four epics - R1 correctness, R2 first journey, R3 surface, R4 scope honesty - so they are claimable rather than a list. R1 is p0 and contains the reproduction script.
